claims.value: The Banco de España held the banknote-issue monopoly for mainland Spain and its islands; Spain did not adopt exclusive gold convertibility.

scope.description: Historical institution or capital of the named polity; monetary statements apply only to the territorial reach explicitly stated, not a polygon-wide statistical measurement.

claims.value: Civil-war Spain had separate Republican and Nationalist issuing institutions and pesetas, each recognised in its own area.

claims.value: The Banco de Portugal operated in a gold-standard financial system, with expanding commercial activity and increasing autonomy.

scope.description: Historical institution or capital of the named polity; monetary statements apply only to the territorial reach explicitly stated, not a polygon-wide statistical measurement.

evidence.note: University institutional history distinguishes recovery at end1850s, subsequent expansion, gold-standard monetary intervention, ending with1891 crisis.

claims.value: After the1891 financial crisis, Portugal left the gold standard and unredeemable banknotes circulated; the Banco de Portugal became more subject to state objectives.

scope.description: Historical institution or capital of the named polity; monetary statements apply only to the territorial reach explicitly stated, not a polygon-wide statistical measurement.

claims.value: The Banque de France held the privilege of issuing banknotes in Paris.

scope.description: Historical institution or capital of the named polity; monetary statements apply only to the territorial reach explicitly stated, not a polygon-wide statistical measurement.

evidence.note: Privilege forParis granted1803; national monopoly obtained1848. Paris privilege is not nationwide monopoly.

claims.value: The Banque de France held the nationwide banknote-issue monopoly after absorbing departmental issuing banks as branches.

scope.description: Historical institution or capital of the named polity; monetary statements apply only to the territorial reach explicitly stated, not a polygon-wide statistical measurement.

evidence.note: Nationwide monopoly granted1848; institutional governance subsequently changed1936. No GDP or statistical territorial equivalence inferred.

claims.value: The1936 reform broadened Banque de France shareholder participation and placed most General Council appointments with public authorities; legal nationalisation followed in December1945.

scope.description: Historical institution or capital of the named polity; monetary statements apply only to the territorial reach explicitly stated, not a polygon-wide statistical measurement.

evidence.note: Source distinguishes1936 de facto governance change from de jure1945 nationalisation. Claim does not present legal nationalisation as already complete.

claims.value: During the Restriction Period, the Bank of England was relieved of its obligation to exchange banknotes for gold.

scope.description: Historical institution or capital of the named polity; monetary statements apply only to the territorial reach explicitly stated, not a polygon-wide statistical measurement.

claims.value: The Bank Charter Act1844 restricted existing note issuers in England and Wales and prohibited new banks from commencing note issue across the United Kingdom.

scope.description: Historical institution or capital of the named polity; monetary statements apply only to the territorial reach explicitly stated, not a polygon-wide statistical measurement.

evidence.note: Source explicitly separates England/Wales restrictions from UK-wide prohibition of new issuers; does not assert early universal monopoly.

qualifications: England/Wales issuing restrictions are not identical to arrangements in Scotland and Ireland.

claims.value: After Britain left the gold standard in1931, holders had no right to convert Bank of England notes into gold or another asset.

scope.description: Historical institution or capital of the named polity; monetary statements apply only to the territorial reach explicitly stated, not a polygon-wide statistical measurement.
